incident-bot: 🔔 PagerDuty: page fired -> service: inference-runtime / check: p95-latency-us-west-2 (threshold 250ms). Incident ID: PD-87321
Alex Chen: acked. I'm on it. :mag:
Maria Gomez: seeing similar alerts from the kv-cache warmup metric - short spikes around 30-90s. no error rate increase yet.
Alex Chen: checking rolling deploys... deploy-bot, any recent rollouts to us-west-2?
deploy-bot: deploy completed for model-router v2.3.1 -> us-west-2 at 2160012200 by kevin.
Kevin Liu: that was a tiny routing tweak, shouldn't affect latency but tagging in case.
Alex Chen: pulling p95 and pod CPU for runtime-service in us-west-2.
Alex Chen: ```
# prometheus-ish
sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="runtime",region="us-west-2"}[1m])) by (le)
```
Maria Gomez: also seeing a KV hit rate increase on a subset of pods. looks like cache misses spiking as new keys warmed. pattern matches a sudden traffic burst from a partner integration.
Samir Patel: can you confirm customer impact? any 5xxs or timeouts?
Maria Gomez: 5xxs stable at baseline, traces show higher tail latency but successful responses. estimated impacted QPS ~120 -> 180 for ~2 mins. few frontends retried, causing secondary tails.
Alex Chen: mitigation plan: 1) pin traffic away from the pod group with high miss rate 2) increase kv-cache warmup parallelism 3) watch for PD re-fires.
Alex Chen: routing change in-flight: scaling up warmup workers + temporarily route 30% traffic to secondary pool. executing now.
Kevin Liu: :thumbsup: initiating traffic shift (k8s rollout pause + service weight change).
Maria Gomez: warming threads showing decreasing miss ratio after ~45s. p95 trending down.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page auto-resolved (PD-87321) after 72s — condition returned to normal.
Alex Chen: leaving the thread open for 5 more minutes to ensure stability; will hand off if it flaps again.
Samir Patel: noted customer-visible latency blips but no error surge; suggest no immediate SEV. track in follow-up doc.
Kevin Liu: we should add a guard to avoid short-lived cache-warmup spikes from firing PD. maybe extend evaluation window to 90s or require concurrent error increase.
Maria Gomez: fwiw the partner traffic pattern is a cold-start fanout every 30m, that's probably triggering. I'll add a short-term smoothing rule.
Alex Chen: thanks. I'll update the oncall postmortem draft with timeline + mitigation.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page fired -> service: inference-runtime / check: p95-latency-us-west-2 (threshold 250ms). Incident ID: PD-87322
Alex Chen: acked PD-87322. looks like a brief re-fire while we were still ramping warmup.
Samir Patel: if that re-fire clears quickly and impact stays small, we can mark it as noisy auto-resolve. make sure ops-runbook updated.
Maria Gomez: second spike resolved in ~54s after additional worker spin-up. p95 normalized.
Alex Chen: handing off to Samir for monitoring window and follow-up doc: Samir, take it? :wave:
Samir Patel: taking it. I'll consolidate metrics, add proposed alert tuning, and create a tiny post-incident task to adjust PD window. assigning to Maria for rule change and Kevin for routing playbook update.
Alex Chen: thanks team. closing active oncall actions. leaving notes: PD-87321/87322 noisy pages due to kv-cache warmup on partner traffic spike; brief p95 elevation, no customer errors. follow-up: adjust alert window, add smoothing, add routing playbook.
Samir Patel: will file the short incident note and link to this thread. :clipboard: anyone want to add anything else?
Kevin Liu: add that the recent model-router tweak increased cold-key fanout by ~8%, so we'll also revisit that config.
Maria Gomez: adding that. good catch.
Alex Chen: :eyes: thanks. I'll mark the thread resolved.
incident-bot: thread closed (incident-bot).
